description: Use case: should an investor buy, sell or hold the shares of ABB Ltd (SIX: ABBN) at the closing price of 28 October 2026, as shown by the system view 'Calculator' for the phrase 'ABB share decision'. The page derives a target price from five valuation methods on the key figures of equity valuation - the earnings multiple (EPS 2027 estimate times a fair P/E), a two-stage discounted cash flow of the free cash flow per share, the enterprise value multiple (operational EBITA 2026 times a fair EV/EBITA minus net debt), the Gordon dividend discount and the analyst consensus - weights them as the reader says, compares the weighted target with the price and turns the upside into the verdict buy, hold or sell with a margin of safety. ABB reports in US dollars and the share is quoted in Swiss francs, so every per-share figure is converted with the USD/CHF rate. The inputs are the price, the EPS estimate 2027, the fair P/E, the free cash flow guidance 2026, the cash flow growth, the required return, the fair EV/EBITA, the analyst consensus target and the margin of safety; the assumptions are the EPS 2026 and trailing, the dividend and its growth, the years and the terminal growth of the cash flow model, the EBITA, the net debt, the shares outstanding, the exchange rate, the holding period and the five method weights. The arguments of the bull and the bear case, the presets, the labels, the hints, the tags, the verdict texts, the sensitivity grid and the sources of the page are the calculator triples and values of 'ABB share decision'. Two numbers need a power that the zukunft.com formulas do not have, the present value factors of the discounted cash flow and the annualised price return, so they are stored as modelled values; all other results are formulas of the file and reproduced by the calc-validation. The inputs that are not measured carry the word assumed and a confidence. State of the data: close of 28 October 2026, Q3 2026 results of 20 October 2026. The page is a model of the key figures, not investment advice.

triples.name: ABB share decision hint
triples.description: ABB Ltd of Zurich sells electrification and automation equipment, reports in US dollars and is quoted in Swiss francs; 1.81 billion shares are outstanding, the market value is about 130 billion CHF [1][9]. The Q3 2026 results of 20 October 2026 brought record orders of 12.1 billion USD and a record operational EBITA margin of 20.8 %, but the adjusted earnings per share missed the consensus by 13 % and the share fell from a 52-week high of 89.14 CHF to 72.88 CHF at the close of 28 October [1][2][9]. Nine analysts rate the share hold with targets from 57 to 88 CHF, on average 77 CHF [3]. Behind the figures lie three portfolio moves: the sale of Robotics to SoftBank for 5.375 billion USD closing in Q4 2026, the 5.5 billion USD offer for the British valve maker Rotork closing in the first half of 2027, and a 51 % stake in Mitsubishi Electric's low-voltage business [1][5][11][13]. Below are the arguments of the bulls and the bears with their numbers, then a calculator: it derives a target price from five valuation methods (earnings multiple, discounted cash flow, enterprise value multiple, dividend discount, analyst consensus), weights them as you say, compares the result with the price - and tells you whether that suggests buying, holding or selling under your assumptions. A model is not investment advice; the assumptions are the decision.

triples.name: ABB share decision model limits
triples.description: one price on one day against estimates that move every quarter; the EPS 2026 consensus may or may not contain the 2.4 billion USD Robotics gain and is used for the PEG only; the Rotork outflow of 2027 and the Robotics inflow of Q4 2026 are not in the net debt; no tax on the dividend, no transaction cost, no portfolio context, no scenario probabilities; the analysts' models, the ABB financial report and the quarterly press releases are the places to look for these

formulas.name: trailing EPS formula
formulas.description: the earnings per share of the last twelve months: the full year 2025 minus the first nine months of 2025 plus the first nine months of 2026

formulas.name: currency conversion per share
formulas.description: ABB reports in US dollars and the share is quoted in Swiss francs, so every per-share figure in USD is multiplied by the USD/CHF rate before it meets the price

formulas.name: earnings multiple target
formulas.description: the target by the earnings multiple: the earnings per share 2027 times the fair price-earnings ratio, in CHF

formulas.name: free cash flow per share formula
formulas.description: the free cash flow of 2026 divided by the shares outstanding; billion USD divided by billion shares gives USD per share, times the exchange rate CHF per share
formulas.expression: "free cash flow per share" = "free cash flow","guidance" / "shares outstanding" * "exchange rate"

formulas.name: net debt per share formula
formulas.description: the net debt divided by the shares outstanding, in CHF
formulas.expression: "net debt per share" = "net debt" / "shares outstanding" * "exchange rate"

formulas.name: discounted cash flow target
formulas.description: two stages: the free cash flow per share grows at the explicit rate for the number of years set and each year's cash flow is discounted at the required return; after the last year a terminal value is the next year's cash flow divided by the required return minus the terminal growth, discounted over the explicit years; the net debt per share is subtracted because the cash flow belongs to the creditors first. The sums of the discount factors of the two stages need a power, which the zukunft.com formulas do not have, so they are stored as the modelled present value factors: the explicit stage factor is the sum over the years t = 1 to n of ((1 + growth) / (1 + return)) to the power of t, the terminal factor is (1 + growth) to the power of n times (1 + terminal growth) divided by (return - terminal growth) divided by (1 + return) to the power of n
formulas.expression: "target price","discounted cash flow" = "free cash flow per share" * ( "present value factor","explicit stage" + "present value factor","terminal growth" ) - "net debt per share"

formulas.name: enterprise value multiple target
formulas.description: the operational EBITA 2026 times the fair EV/EBITA multiple gives the enterprise value; minus the net debt gives the equity value; divided by the shares and converted gives the target per share
formulas.expression: "target price","enterprise value multiple" = ( "operational EBITA" * "fair EV/EBITA" - "net debt" ) / "shares outstanding" * "exchange rate"

formulas.name: dividend discount target
formulas.description: the Gordon growth model: the dividend per share times one plus the growth, divided by the required return minus the growth; undefined if the growth is not below the return

formulas.name: weighted target price formula
formulas.description: each method's target times its weight, summed and divided by the sum of the weights of the methods that produced a value; a method without a value (dividend discount with growth above the return) is left out by the page
formulas.expression: "weighted target price" = ( "target price","earnings multiple" * "weight","earnings multiple" + "target price","discounted cash flow" * "weight","discounted cash flow" + "target price","enterprise value multiple" * "weight","enterprise value multiple" + "target price","dividend discount" * "weight","dividend discount" + "target price","analyst consensus" * "analyst consensus weight" ) / ( "weight","earnings multiple" + "weight","discounted cash flow" + "weight","enterprise value multiple" + "weight","dividend discount" + "analyst consensus weight" )

formulas.name: upside formula
formulas.description: the target divided by the price minus one, as a share; positive means the share is below its target; the percent measure shows it as a percentage

formulas.name: method upside formula
formulas.description: the upside of one method's target against the price, the vs. price column of the method rows

formulas.name: share expected return formula
formulas.description: the annual return if the price reaches the target over the holding period: the annualised price return, a modelled value because it needs the power of one over the years, plus the dividend yield

formulas.name: buy threshold formula
formulas.description: buy below the target divided by one plus the margin of safety

formulas.name: sell threshold formula
formulas.description: sell above the target divided by one minus the margin of safety

formulas.name: trailing P/E formula
formulas.description: the price divided by the last twelve months' EPS in CHF

formulas.name: forward P/E formula
formulas.description: the price divided by the EPS 2027 in CHF

formulas.name: EPS growth formula
formulas.description: the earnings growth from the 2026 estimate to the 2027 estimate, as a share

formulas.name: PEG formula
formulas.description: the forward P/E divided by the earnings growth in percent; the growth is stored as a share, so the factor 100 turns it into the percentage points the PEG convention uses

formulas.name: market capitalisation formula
formulas.description: the price times the shares outstanding; CHF times billion shares gives billion CHF

formulas.name: enterprise value multiple formula
formulas.description: the market capitalisation in USD plus the net debt, divided by the operational EBITA 2026

formulas.name: free cash flow yield formula
formulas.description: the free cash flow per share in CHF divided by the price
formulas.expression: "free cash flow yield" = "free cash flow per share" / "price"

formulas.name: dividend yield formula
formulas.description: the dividend per share divided by the price
